messages:
Ava: Heads up — since ~06:20 UTC we're seeing a spike of GPU pods stuck in Pending in us-west2. Pods show '0/1 GPUs' pending but node allocatable still reports GPUs available. Looks like a slot-shadowing condition after last network blip. Anyone digging in?

matt: yep same. Metrics: host-gpu-12..18 show pods evicted then returned but scheduler not packing new pods. I see taint gpu-isolated=sticky:NoSchedule on some nodes.

leah: I saw a kubelet crash on 10:21 from nodes in that AZ earlier. kubelet re-registered with different topology keys — maybe the scheduler lost affinity metadata and created soft shadows.

jordan: quick check — `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{@.metadata.name}: {.status.allocatable."nvidia.com/gpu"}{"\n"}{end}'` shows GPUs still allocatable. but `kubectl describe node <node>` shows:

```
Taints: gpu-sticky=true:NoSchedule
Annotations:
  scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/gpu-alloc: ring-abc123def
Events:
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume  attach timeout for volume pvc-1234
```

matt: also noticed the scheduler logs show 'no compatible pod' for those slots even though they match resource requests — suspect bound annotation with expired lease (ringbuffer) causing scheduler to treat GPUs as reserved.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled down nodepool-usw2-gpu by 2 at 06:35 — reason: utilization low (0.12).

leah: ops-bot might have removed warm nodes while pods still had PVC/attach or leases — causing orphaned reservations. Workaround: remove taint `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu-sticky=true:NoSchedule-` then trigger descheduler job.

jordan: can we run a targeted descheduler on the affected nodes? I'll queue a job to evict pods with annotation `reservation=shadow`.

matt: patch I ran earlier (temp) — label nodes `gpu-reclaim=true` and run small script to clear stale annotations:

```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu-reclaim=true -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl annotate {} scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/gpu-alloc-
kubectl taint nodes -l gpu-reclaim=true gpu-sticky=true:NoSchedule-
```

leah: after clearing the annotations two nodes accepted new pods within 40s. but still ~12 pods pending. I'm going to coordinate a slow roll of kubelet restarts on the remaining 6 nodes to force lease cleanup. Will post when done.

Ava: thanks — please also add a short postmortem note (incidents channel) and create a ticket to add descheduler rule for expired GPU reservations + a safeguard to prevent autoscaler from scaling down warm nodes with active GPU leases. :+1:

jordan: opened ticket INFRA-1427 with links to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc/gpu-scheduler?orgId=1&panelId=7 and the logs I've collected.

ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-03-21-GPU-SHADOW (assigned eng-platform)
